### Short Answer
The statutory deadline for filing the annual income tax return is on or before the fifteenth (15th) day of April of each year, covering income for the preceding taxable year.

### Controlling Authorities
This requirement is established under Section 51(C)(1) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC).

### Interpretation
Section 51(C)(1) of the NIRC specifies that individuals must file their income tax returns by April 15 each year. This applies to all individuals subject to income tax, ensuring that they report their income for the previous year within the stipulated timeframe.

### Practical Meaning
Taxpayers must ensure that their income tax returns are submitted by the April 15 deadline to avoid penalties and interest for late filing. This deadline is crucial for compliance with tax obligations and maintaining good standing with the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).
